dog.description_text:
AGE / WEIGHT: 11 months old / 31 lbs

GENDER: Female

ENERGY: Moderate to Active

GOOD WITH: Dogs - Yes, Kids - Yes, Cats - TBD

ABOUT ME: See this white paw? People say it looks like a glove, and I use it to say hello to basically everyone on the sidewalk. Strangers tell me I made their day, which honestly tracks. I’m young, goofy, and smart enough to learn fast, though I’ll negotiate a little first. Big dogs are my favorite playmates, Kongs are my favorite snack delivery system, and the leash and I are still working things out.

MY FOSTER SAYS: “Everyone loves her one white paw. A lot of people say it looks like a glove. She has gone up to multiple people who have said to me ‘That just made my day’ after she said hi.”

HISTORY

Sara CLAWs came into rescue in Selma, Alabama, as an older puppy along with her brother; her full history is unknown. She traveled to Brooklyn in early October 2026.

DETAILED PROFILE

Sara CLAWs has a signature accessory: one white paw that strangers keep comparing to a glove. She puts it to good use, marching up to people on the sidewalk to say hello, and more than one has told her foster the greeting made their day. She’s a young, goofy, inquisitive pup who already has a neighborhood fan club.

She’s still settling in, but early signs point to a smart, trainable girl with moderate-to-active energy and plenty of puppy enthusiasm to spend. She can be impressively obedient, with a stubborn streak that appears when she has ideas of her own. She’s also strong for her size; she’s been spotted carrying a ten-pound dumbbell around like a chew toy. For now, she’ll do best with an adopter ready for daily exercise and outdoor exploring.

People are her thing. She’s friendly with everyone, though she still jumps up when excited and is learning to keep four paws on the floor. She’s been comfortable with kids she’s met outside the home; older kids suit her, and younger ones are still to be determined. Other dogs are a highlight. She loves to run, wrestle, and play, especially with medium and large dogs, though she can get overexcited mid-play. A dog sibling would suit her but isn’t required. Cats are unknown.

She’s largely house trained, with an accident or two, and is doing well in her crate. Leash manners are a work in progress; she tends to pull and get distracted on city walks. She likes to chew, so plenty of chew toys and an occasional redirect help. A stuffed Kong is a guaranteed hit.

For anyone who wants a bright, social young dog to train, walk, and show off around the block: the glove comes standard.

MEDICAL HISTORY

The dogs in our care are up-to-date on vaccinations, spayed or neutered (when old enough), microchipped, and given a general health check. Immediate medical needs and medical history will be addressed with the adopter prior to adoption. Complete vet records will be sent shortly after adoption.
dog.name: SARA CLAWS
